# M4: Research Assistant

Branch `feat/m4-research`, worktree `../nt-m4`. Read `STATUS.md` first.
Migration file: `supabase/migrations/20261120000100_research.sql`.

## Goal

An evidence-grounded literature assistant built on Europe PMC and PubMed. **It must work with no
paid AI provider and no LLM at all.** An optional local Ollama model can write nicer summaries.

It must never invent a citation. Every `[n]` marker in an answer must point to a document that
was actually retrieved, and the server checks this.

## Checklist

### API (`api/app/research/`)
- [x] `sources.py`: async `httpx` clients with timeouts, retries on 429 and 5xx (backoff) and a
      descriptive `User-Agent: NeuroTrack/0.1 (open-source research platform)`. **Do not send
      any user email or personal data.** The clients are:
  - Europe PMC REST search (`/europepmc/webservices/rest/search`, `format=json`,
    `resultType=core`).
  - NCBI E-utilities `esearch` + `efetch`/`esummary` (`tool=neurotrack`). Respect the rate
    limit of 3 requests/second without an API key, and accept an optional `NCBI_API_KEY`
    through settings.
- [x] Normalise results to one `Reference` model: `source`, `pmid`, `pmcid`, `doi`, `title`,
      `authors[]`, `journal`, `year`, `abstract`, `publication_types[]`, `url`. Deduplicate
      across sources by PMID or DOI.
- [x] Add an evidence label from the publication type: `systematic-review/meta-analysis`,
      `randomized-trial`, `review`, `primary-study`, `other`. The UI explains it as **the type
      of evidence, not a quality grade**.
- [x] `summarize.py` has a provider interface:
  - **`ExtractiveProvider`** (default; no LLM). Score abstract sentences by overlap with the
    query terms, then build an answer from the top sentences, each tagged `[n]` with its source
    index.
  - **`OllamaProvider`**, used only when `OLLAMA_URL` is set. It is prompted to cite only by
    index and to separate established findings, emerging evidence and open questions.
- [x] Citation validator: parse `[n]` markers and drop any sentence that cites an index which
      wasn't retrieved, or that has no citation at all. Report how many sentences were removed.
      Pytest covers this with adversarial LLM output.
- [x] `GET /research/search?q=&source=all|europepmc|pubmed&limit=` (limit ≤ 25) returns
      `Reference[]`.
- [x] `POST /research/answer {question, max_sources ≤ 8}` returns:
  - `answer_sentences[]` with `citations`.
  - `sources[]`.
  - `provider`.
  - `removed_unsupported`.
  - `disclaimer`.
- [x] Both routes require auth.
- [x] Pytest: all network is mocked with `httpx.MockTransport`; **no live calls in tests**. Cover:
  - Parsing real-shaped fixture JSON and XML for both sources.
  - Dedup.
  - Evidence labels.
  - The extractive summary.
  - The validator.
  - 401 without a token and 422 on bad input.
- [x] Run `pnpm api:types` and commit the generated files.

### Database (one migration)
- [x] `literature_references` is a shared cache. Columns: the normalised fields, a unique key on
      `pmid`/`doi`, `fetched_at`, and a generated `tsvector` over title + abstract with a GIN
      index. RLS: authenticated users can select and insert; nobody can update or delete.
- [x] `saved_references` (`user_id`, `reference_id`, `note`, `created_at`). RLS: own rows only.
- [x] `research_queries` (`user_id`, `query`, `created_at`), as the user's own history. RLS: own
      rows only.
